claims.claim: An exception is an error detected while syntactically valid Python executes; an unhandled exception normally produces an error message and stops execution.
A matching except handler runs after an exception in its try suite, while an unmatched exception propagates outward.
An except clause naming an exception class also matches instances of its subclasses, so handler order matters.
The else suite runs when the try suite completes without an exception, and finally runs as the last task before the try statement completes.
raise accepts an exception instance or a class derived from BaseException; code should normally handle specific expected exception types rather than use a bare except.
